description.text: Flowserve's goal is to create extraordinary flow control solutions to make the world better for everyone. We are a world-leading manufacturer and aftermarket service provider of comprehensive flow control systems. We develop and manufacture precision-engineered flow control equipment integral to the movement, control and protection of the flow of materials in our customers’ critical processes. Our product portfolio of pumps, valves, seals, automation and aftermarket services supports global infrastructure industries, including energy, chemical, power generation and general, which includes water management and pharmaceuticals, where our products and services enable customers to achieve their goals. Through our manufacturing platform and global network of Quick Response Centers ("QRCs"), we offer a broad array of aftermarket equipment services, such as installation, advanced diagnostics and turnkey maintenance programs.

about.description_short: Flowserve Corporation is one of the world's leading providers of fluid motion and control products and services. Operating in more than 50 countries, the Company produces engineered and industrial pumps, seals and valves as well as a range of related flow management services.

employees.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had approximately 16,000 employees (“associates”) globally and a footprint of manufacturing facilities and QRCs in more than 48 countries.

analysis_md:
# FLS — Flowserve Corp
Pass-1 run, 2026-10-20. Engine release 5.5.0. All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Flowserve Corp (NYSE: FLS, SIC 3561 Pumps & Pumping Equipment) — flow-control products and services for global infrastructure: pumps, valves, seals and actuation (Flowserve Pump Division and Flow Control Division), sold into energy, chemical, power (including nuclear), water and general industry, with a large installed-base aftermarket. Price $69.93 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $9.159B — in scope under $40B.

## Owner's earnings
- Conservative definition (OCF − capex − SBC): FY2025 OCF $505,884,000, capex $70,927,000 (PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets), SBC $38,263,000 → latest FY OE total $396.7M, latest FY OE/share $3.03 (key_numbers.md).
- Maintenance definition is reported in financials_history.csv alongside; the conservative OCF-based figure is the one used throughout.
- OE-positive years: 4/5 in the last five (FY2022 OE was negative — OCF was negative that year — which is the cyclicality the scenarios must carry).
- Net debt (latest): $814.9M; net debt / normalized OE 2.15x (key_numbers.md).

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct):**
- OCF: FY $505,884,000 − prior YTD $104,212,000 + current YTD $86,166,000 = TTM $487,838,000
- Capex: FY $70,927,000 − prior YTD $28,340,000 + current YTD $33,807,000 = TTM $76,394,000
- SBC: FY $38,263,000 − prior YTD $18,822,000 + current YTD $20,595,000 = TTM $40,036,000
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): 128,489,000
- **TTM OE total $371,408,000 → base OE/share $2.89** (base_source: ttm_json)
- The normalized (3-yr median) base is $2.37/share and the latest FY is $3.03/share; the TTM base sits between them and is the most current, so it is used. Note FY2025 net income included a $140,092,000 loss on divestiture of asbestos-related assets and liabilities and $195,663,000 of other income in the filed income statement — neither touches the OCF-based conservative OE construction directly, and the TTM OCF leg ($487,838,000) is below the FY2025 OCF leg, so the base is not flattered by FY2025.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow
- FOR: Installed-base aftermarket — record aftermarket bookings of $696 million in Q2 2026 (company release, July 29, 2026), recurring parts/service on a large installed base; Nuclear qualification — content in over 75% of the approximately 400 global reactors, certification and customer approvals that took decades to earn; Global service/distribution network in 50+ countries with severe-service proprietary pump/valve/seal technology.
- AGAINST: Contested project bidding vs Emerson, Sulzer, KSB, ITT, Crane — price and lead-time pressure limits pricing power; Cyclical energy/industrial capex and lumpy large projects — OE was negative in FY2022; ROIC only 5.8–12.7% through the last cycle with no proven wide-moat compounding.
- Evidence (fundamentals.json roic_proxy and gross margin): ROIC proxy FY2020–25: 7.4% / 8.7% / 5.8% / 11.7% / 12.7% / 9.4%; gross margin FY2020–25: 30.0% / 29.6% / 27.5% / 29.6% / 31.5% / 33.4%. Margins are improving, but ROIC has only modestly exceeded the cost of capital through a cycle — a 7+ score is not justified.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-20)
Growth sanity check / recalibration (written reason): the engine blend is 7.20% (rev CAGR 5y 4.87%, rev CAGR 3y 9.37%, latest rev YoY 3.76%, OE/share CAGR 2y 31.61%). The OE/share CAGR is a rebound artefact off depressed FY2022–23, and the latest prints are weaker than 7.20%: Q2 2026 sales were $1,169.2 million, down 1.6% year over year, and management guided FY2026 total sales growth to approximately 3% with organic sales down approximately 1% (adjusted EPS guidance raised to $4.05–$4.20). Scenario starts were therefore recalibrated via offsets −0.12 / −0.07 / −0.04 / +0.01 / +0.06 vs the blend to −4.8% / 0.2% / **3.2%** / 8.2% / 13.2% — the base start matches the company's own total-sales guidance, the bull starts are carried by the Q2 bookings print (total bookings up 25.5% to $1,348.1 million, backlog up 16.9% to $3,336.0 million), not by the blend. Probabilities 10/25/30/25/10; OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 (defaults, no company-specific reason to change them).

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | -4.8% | 0.75 | $13.10 | 4.64% |
| Bear | 25% | 0.2% | 0.90 | $19.38 | 5.89% |
| Base | 30% | 3.2% | 1.00 | $24.41 | 6.89% |
| Bull | 25% | 8.2% | 1.10 | $33.03 | 8.61% |
| Super bull | 10% | 13.2% | 1.25 | $46.10 | 11.04% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $26.35 (−62.3% vs price), IV@12% $34.94, IV@10% $44.51, weighted IRR 7.32%, base-case IRR 6.89%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Tier bear D, tier bull D. Diagnostics: OE yield 4.13%, terminal value 18.6% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.52x, net debt 2.15x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): 15% at $26.35, 20% at $18.62, 25% at $14.36.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, quoted above (TTM OE/share $2.89 vs latest FY $3.03 and median $2.37).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023): resolved from the FY2023 cash-flow statement (10-K): net earnings including noncontrolling interests were $205,188,000 against OCF of $325,772,000. The gap is principally non-cash addbacks — depreciation $73,464,000 and amortization $10,283,000 plus stock-based compensation $27,808,000 in that statement — together with working-capital and other lines in the same statement (accrued liabilities +$59,213,000, accounts payable +$53,065,000, retirement obligations +$38,497,000, contract liabilities +$26,837,000, partly offset by inventories −$59,831,000, contract assets −$41,149,000 and net deferred taxes −$62,841,000). No single one-off tax deposit or impairment drives it; the OCF-based conservative OE is the series used throughout, so the divergence does not contaminate the base.
- Preliminary-run **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (4.5x on default starts): no longer present in the final run — the recalibrated spread is 3.52x. Confidence is still held at medium, not high, given the cyclical OE history (negative FY2022).

## Thoughts / method range
- Even the super-bull scenario (13.2% growth start, 1.25x OE) yields only an 11.04% IRR at $69.93 — no defensible scenario mix on this base clears 15% at the current price. The verdict is not assumption-sensitive in direction: the preliminary run on the median base ($2.37/share) and default starts also printed Tier D (weighted IRR 7.26%).
- The market price embeds the margin-expansion / backlog story (Q2 adjusted operating margin 15.3%, bookings +25.5%, backlog $3,336.0 million, raised EPS guidance) at a level the owner's-earnings cash flows do not support at a 15% hurdle: OE yield is only 4.13%.
- Leverage is manageable (net debt $814.9M, 2.15x normalized OE) and buybacks are modest (share count CAGR −0.09%); neither changes the verdict.
- Balance-sheet note for the final filing check: long-term debt rose in H1 2026 on acquisition-related financing per Q2 reporting; the scored net debt is the FY2025 filing figure ($814.9M) quoted above — if anything, higher current debt would lower, not raise, the IV.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 7.32% on the TTM base; bear→bull band D→D)
- Confidence: **Medium**
- One-liner: Decent-quality flow-control maker, moat 5/10 — does not clear 15% at $69.93 (weighted IRR 7.32%, IV@15% $26.35; clears 15% only below ~$26.35)
